title: One-third noise stability bound
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $\alpha\in\mathbb R$. Suppose $f(x)\in\{0,1\}$ for every $x$ and its uniform mean on the cube is $\alpha$. Choose $X$ uniformly from the cube, and form $Y$ by independently keeping each coordinate of $X$ with probability $2/3$ and flipping it with probability $1/3$. Then $\mathbb E[f(X)f(Y)]\leq \alpha^{3/2}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
